title: Are Causal Neuron Circuits Unique and Transferable?
abstract: arXiv:2611.13885v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Interpretability demonstrations often show that intervening on a group of neurons changes a model's answer. A recent example removes an 18-neuron group in Qwen3-32B and the model answers "Simba" instead of "Scar" to a two-hop Lion King riddle. Such a demonstration establishes that the group matters, but not how much of it is necessary, whether other groups could do the same, or whether the effect carries over to other inputs. We ask: when intervening on a group of neurons changes a model's answer, how much of that group is actually necessary? For every selected group we measure all 4,096 subsets of 12 MLP neurons. On a two-alternative capital task (Qwen3-0.6B), zero-ablating 12 selected neurons lowers the answer margin by 27% while random neurons barely change it, yet replacing the same neurons with their values from other questions also barely changes it: their activations are nearly constant across questions, and we find no evidence

translated_title: 因果神经元回路是唯一且可迁移的吗？
translated_abstract: 可解释性领域的演示常常表明，对一组神经元进行干预会改变模型的回答。最近的一个例子是：移除 Qwen3-32B 中的一组 18 个神经元后，模型对一个两跳《狮子王》谜语的回答从“刀疤”变成了“辛巴”。这类演示证明了该神经元组确实重要，但没有说明其中有多少神经元是真正必要的、其他神经元组是否能起到同样作用，以及这种效应是否会迁移到其他输入上。我们提出的问题是：当对一组神经元的干预改变了模型的回答时，这组神经元中究竟有多少是必要的？对于每个选定的神经元组，我们测量了 12 个 MLP 神经元全部 4,096 种子集的效果。在一个二选一的首都识别任务（Qwen3-0.6B）上，将 12 个选定神经元置零会使答案置信边际下降 27%，而随机神经元几乎不产生改变；然而，用其他问题中的激活值替换这同一批神经元同样几乎不改变结果：这些神经元的激活在不同问题之间几乎恒定，我们没有找到证据（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过穷举测量 12 个 MLP 神经元全部 4,096 种子集的干预效果，发现虽然消融选定神经元组会显著改变模型回答，但这些神经元的激活在不同问题间几乎恒定、替换后也几乎无影响，说明真正必要的只是其中一部分，从而质疑了因果神经元回路的唯一性与可迁移性。
en_tdlr: By exhaustively measuring all 4,096 subsets of 12 MLP neurons, this paper finds that although ablating a selected neuron group changes the model's answer, the neurons' activations are nearly constant across inputs and replacing them has little effect, indicating only part of the group is necessary and questioning the uniqueness and transferability of causal neuron circuits.
